title: When to swing and when to stop
target: How to use a melee weapon in R.E.P.O. without wasting one, given that the game gives melee weapons durability, a hit freeze and a swing you can aim.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A melee weapon in the crew
Charge in it if it needs any
A monster you intend to hit rather than avoid

steps.do: Accept that a melee weapon wears out as you use it.
steps.because: melee weapons drain durability on hits (durabilityDrainOnEnemiesAndPVP)

steps.do: Check the weapon over after a fight rather than assuming it is fine.
steps.because: a melee weapon can have a broken mesh of its own (hasBrokenMesh)

steps.do: Face what you are hitting, since the weapon records its hitting side.
steps.because: there is a hitting side angle and a forward tilt (hittingSideAngle)

steps.do: Expect a moment of freeze on impact and use it.
steps.because: the game keeps a hit freeze with its own delay (hitFreezeDelay)

steps.do: Remember that some melee weapons run on battery.
steps.because: a melee weapon can be set to use battery logic (usesBatteryLogic)

commonMistakes: Swinging a spent weapon and wondering why nothing happens.
Hitting sideways without facing the target.
Forgetting a battery-powered melee weapon needs charge.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
